title: Storage adapter selection for project P
context: Project P requires a reversible storage adapter selection. Externally issued authority gov://P/grants/G-17 authorizes actor SARCHI to select one reversible storage adapter candidate at A2 ceiling, candidate-only, bound to exact target project-P digest sha256:T against baseline main digest sha256:B, valid 2026-08-01 through 2026-08-31, not revoked and not previously consumed. Verified facts: the authority reference is externally issued, current, scope-matched to project, decision type, target, and baseline. Reported facts: option trade-offs are as supplied in the request and were not independently benchmarked. Assumption: the adapter interface remains reversible so either option can be replaced without data-model lock-in. No mutation, merge, publication, deployment, activation, risk acceptance, evidence acceptance, or promotion is authorized by this artifact.

options.name: PostgreSQL
options.summary: Client-server relational engine used as the storage adapter for project P.
tradeoffs: Durable multi-process concurrency suitable for concurrent writers
Higher operational cost: provisioning, backup, upgrade, and monitoring burden
Adds an external service dependency to local and CI environments

options.name: SQLite
options.summary: Embedded file-based relational engine used as the storage adapter for project P.
tradeoffs: Simple to operate with no separate service to run
Weaker multi-process concurrency under concurrent writers
Low operational cost and trivial local/CI setup

options.name: Do nothing
options.summary: Defer adapter selection and keep the baseline main sha256:B unchanged.
tradeoffs: No migration effort and no new operational surface
Consumes no authority but blocks dependent design work

consequences: Positive: durable multi-process concurrency addresses the concurrent-writer requirement that SQLite does not meet.
Negative: increases operational cost and introduces an external service dependency for local, CI, and production-like environments.
Reversibility: the selection is reversible at the adapter boundary; no data-model lock-in is recorded and rollback is a return to baseline main sha256:B.
Migration: any schema or data migration is out of scope of this artifact and requires separate implementation authority.
This artifact is CANDIDATE and NOT_EFFECTIVE; it grants no mutation, merge, deployment, activation, or promotion authority.
evidence_refs: request-supplied option trade-offs: PostgreSQL durable concurrency with operational cost
request-supplied option trade-offs: SQLite simple with weaker multi-process concurrency

Target project-P digest changes from sha256:T or baseline main changes from sha256:B
